criteria.evidence: Delta 8095a02..d7c8c4c touches no schema or id rule. Full suite at d7c8c4c (git archive copy, temporary local Postgres 16): node --test 572/572; tsc --noEmit passes; eslint and prettier pass on every changed file.

Both delta findings fixed. Finding 1 (skill id joins any group): tailoring-pipeline.ts:234 'entryOf.get(id) ?? "skills"'. Verbatim copies of summaryPasses at 8095a02 and d7c8c4c: 'Data Analyst at Initech with SQL.' [EXP-01, skill:SQL] PASS -> null; 'Data analyst with SQL.' [SUM-01, skill:SQL] PASS -> null; 'Excel, SQL.' and 'Data Analyst at Initech. Excel, SQL.' stay PASS. Finding 2 (period inside a name): tailoring-pipeline.ts:205 sentenceBreak; with EXP-01 organization 'Initech Pvt. Ltd.', 'Data Analyst at Initech Pvt. Ltd. with Kotlin.' [EXP-01, PRJ-01-1] PASS -> null, 'Infosys Ltd. with Kotlin' and 'Yahoo! with Kotlin' PASS -> null, the honest 'Data Analyst at Initech Pvt. Ltd. with Excel.' [EXP-01, EXP-01-1] stays PASS. New tests on old code: the d7c8c4c summary-skills file run against 8095a02 code fails 1 test, on 'Data Analyst at Initech with SQL.' only. With s-entry-skill removed it passes 18/18 on 8095a02, so s-abbreviation does not fail on old code (finding 1).

(2) Sentence break. New split points are a strict subset of the old ones (old split at every . ! ? not before a digit; new only before whitespace plus an uppercase letter, or at the end). clauseBreak is unchanged, and a merged sentence needs ONE group for the union of its clauses, so a merge can only reject more, never bypass D37. Merges reject some honest summaries: 'Data Analyst at Initech. dbt, SQL.' and '... Initech. kotlin.' go PASS -> null (lowercase-start skill names); 'e.g. SQL' was already null at both heads (the words e and g are in no fact). All null, so fail closed. Residual wrong split, at both heads, not a regression: an abbreviation before a capital ('U.S. Bank', 'Pvt. Ltd', 'St. Xavier') still splits. It bypasses D37 only when every word after the split belongs to one other group: org 'U.S. Bank' plus PRJ-01-1 'Built a bank app in Kotlin.' makes 'Data Analyst at U.S. Bank with Kotlin.' PASS at both. Without that coincidence it is null. Accepted as residual: the verifier still checks, and the D37 cost of a general fix is high. Note: docs/architecture.md:285 says 'Pvt. Ltd.' stays in one sentence. It does not: the text splits after 'Pvt.'. The case is rejected only because 'Ltd' anchors the tail to EXP-01 (see finding 1). (3) '?? "skills"': summaryFacts holds only entries, bullets, skill:<name> and the summary. An unknown id, such as an answer id, fails 'cited.length !== draft.sourceIds.length' (verified: [EXP-01, ANS-01] is null). The summary id maps to its own group. Stated skill ids are filtered out before grouping. So only non-stated resume skills reach 'skills'. Pre-existing, outside the delta, follow-up only: an entry or bullet id spelled 'skill:<name>' passes the uniqueness check (facts.ts superRefine excludes skill ids) and takes the skill's text with the entry's group. 'Data Analyst at Initech with Kotlin.' [EXP-01, skill:Kotlin] then passes at both heads if a bullet of EXP-01 has id 'skill:Kotlin'. The app does not generate such ids. Nit: line 237's filter(group !== undefined), line 248's '[undefined]' fallback and line 252's 'set.group === undefined' are now unreachable.

(4) Test replacement. The stored-row test keeps the exact sorted-key deepEqual, now ['bullets','generationId','skills','summary']. The leak loop over the non-result columns (Acme Corp, Senior Analyst, Initech, Data Analyst, Excel) is unchanged: the diff touches 2 lines of the file. The golden helper is still an exact assert.equal. Fixture diff: only key 'tailoring-generate' changes, and SequenceMatcher shows a single insertion equal to the clause at tailoring-pipeline.ts:90. 'tailoring-repair' is byte-identical. The new test name ('...generate prompt differs from main only by the skills clause and the repair prompt equals main') is accurate. Both tests failed at 8095a02 and pass at d7c8c4c.

(5) Privacy. tailormyresume_tailorings.result now also holds summary text and skill names derived from the profile. That is the same class of data as the tailored bullets it already held. Only the owner can GET it, it is purged 24 h after finished_at, and DELETE /v1/me cascades it. Constitution I.5 governs device-to-backend egress and is not affected. No profile text reaches a non-result column (the leak loop passes). Acceptable. Only the compliance record understates the column (finding 2).

findings.title: The s-abbreviation case passes on 8095a02, so the sentence-break fix has no regression test, and the docs misstate why it works
findings.trigger: The test profile's EXP-01 organization is 'Initech', so 'Pvt' is in no cited fact. 'Data Analyst at Initech Pvt' fails the content check under either regex. Verified: the d7c8c4c test file without s-entry-skill passes 18/18 against 8095a02 code. Reverting line 205 to /[.!?](?!\p{N})/u keeps the suite green. The real case needs the organization 'Initech Pvt. Ltd.' (copy at 8095a02 PASS, at d7c8c4c null). Separately, docs/architecture.md:285 says 'so "Pvt. Ltd." stays in one sentence'. The regex splits after 'Pvt.'. The draft is rejected because the tail 'Ltd. with Kotlin' must rest on one group. Fix: run s-abbreviation with a profile whose EXP-01 organization is 'Initech Pvt. Ltd.' (or use 'Infosys Ltd. with Kotlin', which never splits). Reword the doc to 'split only before whitespace and an uppercase letter, or at the end'.
